title: Problem Overview
content:
**Erdős Problem #110: Chromatic Number Growth in Uncountable Graphs**

Conjecture: For ℵ₁-chromatic graphs, there exists F(n) bounding the size of n-chromatic subgraphs.

**Answer**: NO - DISPROVED by Lambie-Hanson (2020) in ZFC.

Key history: de Bruijn-Erdős (1951) → Erdős-Hajnal-Szemerédi conjecture (1982) → Shelah consistency (2005) → Lambie-Hanson ZFC disproof (2020).
mathContext: This problem sits at the intersection of infinite graph theory and set theory, connecting chromatic numbers to cardinal arithmetic.
prerequisites: the chromatic number of a graph
cardinal numbers and the axiom system ZFC

title: Graph Coloring Definitions
content:
**IsProperColoring:** Adjacent vertices get different colors.

**IsKColorable:** Admits a proper k-coloring.

**chromaticNumber:** Minimum k for k-colorability (as ℕ∞).

**inducedSubgraph:** Restriction of G to vertex subset S.

**HasFiniteNChromaticSubgraph(G, n, bound):** G has an n-chromatic subgraph on ≤ bound vertices.
mathContext: These definitions set up the framework for studying chromatic properties of finite subgraphs of infinite graphs.
prerequisites: graph coloring and the chromatic number

title: Cardinals and Infinite Chromatic Numbers
content:
**aleph0, aleph1:** ℵ₀ (countable infinity) and ℵ₁ (first uncountable cardinal).

**HasChromaticNumberAtLeast(G, κ):** Not k-colorable for any k < κ.

**HasChromaticNumber(G, κ):** Chromatic number is exactly κ.

The conjecture specifically targets ℵ₁-chromatic graphs.
mathContext: ℵ₁ = succ(ℵ₀) is the first uncountable cardinal. The conjecture's failure for ℵ₀ was already known.
prerequisites: cardinal numbers and aleph notation ℵ

title: de Bruijn-Erdős Theorem
content:
**de_bruijn_erdos (1951):** If χ(G) ≥ ℵ₀, then for every n, G contains a finite n-chromatic subgraph.

**de_bruijn_erdos_compactness:** The compactness formulation—if every finite subgraph is k-colorable, so is G.

**Crucial limitation:** These say nothing about the SIZE of n-chromatic subgraphs!
mathContext: The de Bruijn-Erdős theorem is a compactness result. It guarantees existence but not uniform bounds, which is exactly the gap the conjecture tried to fill.
prerequisites: the chromatic number of infinite graphs

title: The Erdős-Hajnal-Szemerédi Conjecture
content:
**ErdosHajnalSzemerediConjecture (1982):** For ℵ₁-chromatic graphs, there exists F : ℕ → ℕ such that for large n, an n-chromatic subgraph exists on ≤ F(n) vertices.

**conjecture_fails_aleph0:** Already known to fail for ℵ₀-chromatic graphs.

The conjecture tried to leverage ℵ₁ > ℵ₀ to obtain uniform bounds.
mathContext: The hope was that uncountable chromatic number would be 'strong enough' to guarantee efficient finite approximations.

title: Shelah's Consistency and Lambie-Hanson's ZFC Disproof
content:
**shelah_consistency (2005):** Consistent with ZFC that no F exists.

**lambie_hanson_counterexample (2020):** Proved in ZFC—no extra assumptions. Constructed an ℵ₁-chromatic graph defeating every proposed bound F.

**erdos_110_disproved:** Direct proof that ¬ErdosHajnalSzemerediConjecture by extracting the counterexample and deriving contradiction.
mathContext: Shelah's consistency result left open whether this was a ZFC theorem. Lambie-Hanson's construction settled this definitively.

title: Lambie-Hanson Graph Structure
content:
**LambieHansonGraph:** A structure capturing the three key properties:
1. χ(G) = ℵ₁ exactly
2. Defeats all proposed bounds F
3. Still has n-chromatic subgraphs (by de Bruijn-Erdős)

**lambie_hanson_graph_exists:** Proved from the counterexample axiom and de Bruijn-Erdős.
mathContext: The existence proof combines Lambie-Hanson's counterexample with de Bruijn-Erdős to show all three properties hold simultaneously.

title: Summary
content:
**erdos_110:** ¬ErdosHajnalSzemerediConjecture (the conjecture is FALSE).

**erdos_110_summary:** Combines the disproof with the existence of the counterexample graph:
```lean
⟨erdos_110_disproved, lambie_hanson_graph_exists⟩
```

The answer to Problem #110 is NO: no uniform bound F(n) exists.
mathContext: A complete resolution via counterexample, answering a question that stood open for nearly 40 years (1982-2020).
prerequisites: the proof technique of the disproof
